commits.summary: Alignment A1: the ground truth of the hand-written mappings in examples 121-139, part by part, anchored or internal
commits.body: examples/tools/alignment/ground-truth.json breaks the mappings people wrote for the B9 examples 121-139 (--before-target, --before-arguments, --results-agree-when) into parts: one per renamed or moved method, per old input (the receiver first), per new input without a counterpart, and per result. Each input is anchored (the same parameter in both versions, whose mapping is fixed to itself: where an offset mapping must be impossible), internal (a representation that changed, which inference may relate) or new (left free); each result is equal, compared by component (a record that gained one), or changed (a person's decision). Scopes are recorded as a person's decisions, not mappings. 19 examples, 85 parts. The page examples/tools/alignment/README.md defines the scores later steps get against it: found, asked, wrong, missed, and wrong-and-accepted counted on its own.

commits.summary: Alignment A2: jvmcontract align proposes method correspondence between two builds, ranked, written to the hints file
commits.body:
A new module, lib/src/alignment.rs, and the command jvmcontract align --before DIR --after DIR [--hints FILE] [--json]. It works statically and proves nothing. An old method the new build declares with the same class, name and descriptor corresponds to itself and to nothing else. For a vanished one, the candidates are the new build's new methods tied to it by the same name (in its class or moved), the same body shape, a similar body, a caller in common, or the same parameters in the same class. Each tie adds weight to a score. The first candidate leads only with at least 3 points and 3 ahead of the next; otherwise the choice is a person's. --hints replaces the file's inferred proposals and keeps every hint a person stated or approved. Hint gains two optional fields, rank and why (the shared IR, added only; the golden files are unchanged).

Scored on the A1 ground truth with the new examples/tools/alignment.py score, recorded in examples/tools/alignment/scores/A2-methods.json and on its page. Methods that kept their name: 15 of 15 found. Moved: 2 of 2 found. Renamed: 1 found, 1 asked (122, whose only tie is its parameters). Nothing was wrong or missed. Caveat: the same-parameters tie and the lead threshold were set after a first run, and the table and the scorer come from this stream, so the score shows agreement with the table, not generality. Verified with 2 unit tests and 7 tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs on javac-compiled pairs and the joint example's kernel, and 15 Python tests in test_alignment.py; the foundations integration test still passes (alignment still unsupported there until A4's field correspondence). lib/README.md documents the command.

All four are other streams' commits (summaries S1 and S2a, heap H1, observations O1) that check sees in the shared repository; none is on this branch, and their manifests are in their own workspaces. commits.summary: Alignment A3 (static half): align maps each matched pair's arguments, records and result under the preservation contract, scored on examples 121-139
commits.body:
jvmcontract align now relates, for every method pair it matches, how each old input is made from the new inputs and how the results compare, in the form --before-arguments and --results-agree-when take (lib/src/alignment/mappings.rs). It works under the comparison's preservation contract (the new --contract option, or for a standalone method the one its two signatures imply): an input the contract fixes is mapped to itself and nothing else, a stated derivation is used as stated, and candidates are only names, field paths, an integral cast and records built with their constructors, never arithmetic, so the offset mapping before.c = after.c + 1 cannot be proposed. Internal inputs (a parameter gathered into a record, a record that gained a component) are ranked by name, type and position, a weak or tied match is a question, and new inputs nothing uses are left free. Results come from a small catalogue (equal, widened, wrapped or unwrapped, compared on the old components, or a changed meaning put to a person as a question), and every required observation stays in the accounting. Proposals go to the hints file as inferred, proposed, unchecked correspondences.

Verified with 8 new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs (the planted offset case with and without a contract among them), 4 in examples/tools/test_alignment.py, and the whole cargo suite; the integration contract still reports alignment as unsupported, now naming A4. Scored on the A1 table (examples/tools/alignment/scores/A3-mappings.json): 50 of 50 anchored inputs, 8 of 8 internal, 4 of 4 new inputs left free, 17 of 17 inferred results found, and the 2 changed results (122, 123) asked; nothing wrong or missed, and the proposals amount to the examples' own hand-written flags. The rules were written with that table in view, so this shows consistency, not generality. No proofs yet: checking proposals by the regression proof is A3's second half, after A4's narrow case.

commits.summary: Alignment Progress: name the sync.py check errors after A3's static half, none of them this stream's
commits.body: After the A3 commit, sync.py check lists 18 errors: more of the other streams' commits without a manifest in this workspace, and five of the planning session's launch commits from before the fork, which point at a log their manifest does not list. None is on this stream's work, and the traces they concern are outside what a stream may edit; the Progress section names them for the reconcile loop. No code changed.

commits.summary: Alignment A4 (narrow case): field correspondence from constructor routing; align::propose passes the joint example's alignment checks
commits.body:
New lib/src/alignment/fields.rs relates a class that changed shape between two builds field by field. It reads which fields each version's constructor sets straight from a parameter, pairs the old constructor with the one the method correspondence (A2) matched, and maps the old constructor's parameters by A3's rules: names, types, positions, record components, integral casts, never arithmetic. Composing those gives an equation per old field, for the joint example old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents and old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity. An anchored object input stays fixed to itself and only its internal fields are related. A field set any other way (computed, wrapped in a new object, shifted by a constant) is named unsupported, and nothing partial is proposed. In the hints file the field equations replace the input's own equation in the correspondence. lib/src/spec/align.rs's propose now loads both builds, aligns them under the contract and returns the hints, or Unsupported naming the gaps when the subject's mapping is incomplete.

Verified inline: lib/tests/foundations.rs reports alignment propose after and alignment propose offset as passed (2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed). after gets the golden correspondence; offset gets the same equations and no shifted input. Three new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs: the kernel (with the contract, standalone, and through propose), a renamed field with a new one left free, and constructors that wrap or shift the value, never related. All 17 alignment tests and the whole cargo suite pass. The A2 and A3 scores on examples 121-139 are unchanged and re-recorded under the new tool's hash. Shared files changed: lib/README.md (the align paragraph and the module sentence) and lib/tests/alignment.rs.

commits.summary: Alignment A3 (second half): align --prove checks every proposal by the regression proof, collapses by proof, and settles each pair (verification pending)
commits.body:
jvmcontract align --prove (lib/src/alignment/proofs.rs) runs the regression check (equivalence::run, as a caller) on every complete mapping align proposes for a pair, with the flags it amounts to, under the scope and proof options given. A vacuous proof counts as none. Proved mappings with the same result relation are collapsed into one candidate: each makes the old version's observations a function of the new one's on every input of the claim, so nothing a consumer sees tells them apart. Each pair is then settled: one proved (evidence 'proved for claim key K', intent still proposed; for a standalone method, the relation is proved and whether it is the intended one is unconfirmed; for a changed result, approving it is a person's decision), several relations proved (a question), or none (each mapping tried, with its counterexample). The hints file carries each proposal's evidence. The claim key is provisional (a digest of the tool, both builds' class files, the flags and settings) until the summaries stream's canonical key exists. Field-equation proposals are not tried: they have no flag form, and their proof is the heap stream's.

The brief says collapse is for candidates that give every external input the same old-side value; this collapses by observations, which is weaker and is what the outside review's rationale asks for (no question between mappings with no observable difference).

Verified inline: 5 new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs, run by the own checker on one-line methods (the offset defect refuted with no mapping hiding it; a type-only question settled by the one mapping that holds; a sum's two orders collapsed; a changed result with two proved relations asked; the outcome rules on made-up attempts), 22 pass; 4 new scorer tests in examples/tools/test_alignment.py, 23 OK; the static scores on 121-139 unchanged (re-recorded under the new tool hash); the full cargo suite passes; the integration contract 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed.

Verification pending: job 20261107-053806-alignment-a3-second-half-every-proposal (verification/jobs/, quick, priority 10) runs alignment.py score --step proofs over examples 121-139 and should find every verified example's hand-written mapping proved, no mapping proved for any violation, and nothing wrong and accepted.

It is listed for review, with the result it should give: every verified example's hand-written mapping proved, no mapping proved for any violation, nothing wrong and accepted. Also notes the 24 sync.py check errors, none of them this stream's commits. The next step is the rest of A4.

commits.summary: Alignment A4: field correspondence through value objects a constructor makes, and a method moved into one
commits.body:
Field correspondence (lib/src/alignment/fields.rs) now follows a field set to a new object made from parameters passed straight, e.g. this.amount = new Money(cents), into that class's own constructor, to three levels deep. That gives old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents, nested paths such as new.q.amount.c.v, and the reverse old.q.amount.cents == new.q.cents. Anything computed (new Money(cents * 2), cents + 1, a constant an old value object's constructor sets) is named and not related.

A method moved into the value object (the joint example's Quote#cents to Money#cents, whose receivers differ) is now mapped. If the old method only reads fields of its object, and the class's correspondence puts all of them inside one field of the new class, a new input of that field's class stands for the old object: old.this.cents == new.this.cents. Fields the old method never reads (quantity) are named in the mapping and the hint's why, and no equation relates them. FieldCorrespondence gains within and unread, both serde-defaulted. A note for the reconcile loop is under Progress: correspondences can now leave old fields unconstrained, and the IR doc doesn't say so yet.

Verified inline: the old A4 test that held a constructed value object never related is replaced (that was the gap closed here) by 4 tests covering wrapped, nested, unwrapped, shifted, computed, old-constant, the kernel's moved Quote#cents, and a moved method reading a field the value object doesn't keep. All 25 tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs pass, as do the full cargo suite and test_alignment.py. The integration contract gives 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed. The static scores on 121-139 are unchanged and re-recorded under the new tool hash. Shared files: lib/README.md (the align comment) and lib/tests/alignment.rs. The brief's text above Progress still holds.

commits.summary: Alignment A4: nested shapes, a field whose own class changed shape related through that class
commits.body:
Field correspondence (lib/src/alignment/fields.rs) now follows an old field set from a constructor parameter whose own class changed shape into that class's correspondence, prefixed with where the new constructor stores the parameter: a Q holding an L whose cents became amount.cents gives old.q.line.cents == new.q.line.amount.cents. A candidate is as sure as the less sure of its two steps, the inner class's free fields are free at their paths, and an inner gap leaves the outer field unsupported with the gap named. Followed to three levels; a class holding its own class (N next) needs a relation over a chain of objects and is named, not followed. same_shape in mappings.rs is now deep (members' types, array elements, cycles taken as the same), so such a Q is no longer anchored by its signatures alone, and a result of such a class is no longer called equal: it is a person's decision until results get output equations.

Verified: one more test in lib/tests/alignment.rs (nested with a free inner field, an inner shift never related, a chain named), all 26 pass, and the whole cargo suite; the integration contract on this branch gives 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed; the Python scoring tests pass; the static score on examples 121-139 is unchanged, re-recorded under the new tool's hash. Also fixes an ambiguous rustdoc link in alignment.rs. The brief's Progress is updated; nothing else in it is out of date.

commits.summary: Alignment A4: a result whose class changed shape compared field by field, from the class's field correspondence
commits.body:
A method returning an object of a class whose shape changed between the builds (Quote's cents became amount.cents) no longer has its result left 'changed', a person's decision. align now compares it by the same field correspondence its inputs are related by: each old field at its path in the new object, as the relation previous.cents == result.amount.cents && previous.quantity == result.quantity (a new result kind, fields), written to the hints file as Correspondence.outputs. Only paths and integral casts, and only primitive fields: a reference field (a String) would be compared by object id across two runs, so it leaves the result a person's decision with the gap named, as does a field the constructors can't relate (a shift). align --prove doesn't try such a proposal: the regression check can't observe an object result, and that proof is the heap stream's.

Verified: a new test in lib/tests/alignment.rs (the relation, its accounting, its hint's outputs, no proof attempted; a shifted and a String field left a person's decision with the gap named); all 27 alignment tests, the unit, conformance, foundations and skill suites pass; test_alignment.py 23 OK; the integration contract 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed; static scores on 121-139 unchanged, re-recorded under the new hash. In tests/integration.rs one test failed, the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs: JBMC on fixtures.Pricing#total hit its time limit after 615 s with the other loops running. It runs no alignment code and was not repeated inline.

commits.summary: Alignment A4: unchanged code over a class that changed shape is reshaped, not unchanged, and mapped through the class
commits.body:
A2 counted a method unchanged when its code and access flags were the same, so Pricing#withQuantity(Quote, int) and Quote#quantity() in the joint example got no mapping, though the Quote they take and return changed shape (cents became amount.cents). Such a method is now a new change kind, reshaped, matched to itself, and A3/A4 map it like a changed method: withQuantity's q is related field by field (old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents, old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity), quantity anchored, and its result compared by the class's field correspondence; Quote#quantity's receiver is related the same way. A method over classes that kept their shape is still unchanged. A reshaped method over a class whose constructor shifts what it stores is named and gets no proposal. With this, every item of A4 is done.

Verified: a new test in lib/tests/alignment.rs, and the A2 kernel test that asserted withQuantity unchanged (the gap closed here) now asserts reshaped; all 28 pass, with the unit (185), foundations (3), skill (1) and conformance suites, and every test target compiles. tests/integration.rs was not rerun inline: it runs no alignment code, and its JBMC case timed out under load last cycle. Integration contract on this branch: 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed. Scores on examples 121-139 unchanged, re-recorded under the new tool hash. Progress names the shared files changed (lib/README.md, lib/tests/alignment.rs) and two cases A5 starts with.

commits.summary: Alignment A5: each decision that is a person's put as a question, with its candidates, what each means, and a one-line approve that sets intent only
commits.body:
A hint that answers a person's decision now carries an ask (spec::Ask: what to decide, and what approving this candidate would settle, part by part), and is ranked even when it is the only candidate. What is asked: an input or field whose candidates none leads (several and none ahead, or one on type alone), a result whose meaning changed, a vanished method with no leading candidate; after align --prove, what the proof leaves open (several relations proved, or every candidate refuted), while one proved settles it. jvmcontract align now ends with its questions, read from the hints file after the merge: each decision, every candidate with what it means and its evidence (the counterexample where a proof refuted it), and the one line that approves it. The new jvmcontract approve command sets the chosen proposal's intent to approved and nothing else, drops the subject's other proposals of that kind, and refuses a decided subject, a missing one, or an unnamed choice among several. A subject a person decided is not asked again, so a hints file whose decisions are all approved asks nothing.

Also fixed, the two cases A4 left for A5 (seen on the joint example's kernel compiled without parameter names): a lone field candidate on type alone is still one proposal but now asked as a question; and a new field reached only by a question's candidate is no longer called free. free is now what no candidate reaches, and a new open list (on Mapping and FieldCorrespondence) is what only some reach, so each proposal and each result candidate names what it leaves uncompared.

Verified: 31 tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs pass (3 new: the lone candidate on the nameless kernel, approve through the command then reruns asking 2 and then nothing, approve's refusals; questions asserted in 4 existing ones), and the unit (185), foundations (3), skill (1) and conformance (9, 2 ignored) suites; every test target compiles; the Python tests pass; the integration contract on this branch: 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed. Scores on examples 121-139 unchanged, re-recorded under the new tool's hash. Shared files changed: lib/src/spec/mod.rs (Hint.ask and Ask, serde-defaulted and skipped when empty; rank's doc), lib/src/main.rs (approve, and the questions in align's output), lib/README.md, lib/tests/alignment.rs. Left for A5's second step, under Progress: an approved hint's evidence going stale when the claim key changes, approved-but-unproved hints listed, and an input that separates two proved relations.

commits.summary: Alignment A5: an approved relation's evidence comes from a proof under the current claim key, goes stale when it no longer matches, and approved-but-unproved decisions are listed
commits.body:
Every align --hints run now works out each proposed relation's claim key under the current builds and proof settings (lib/src/alignment/evidence.rs). Each hint a person approved or stated then takes the evidence of this run's proof of the same relation. Otherwise it keeps proved or refuted evidence only while that claim key is still one the current builds, flags and settings give, and is marked stale once it isn't: a change to either build, another tool binary, or other proof settings. An approved method takes its pair's proof evidence. align lists every decision a person made that isn't proved under the current key (unchecked, stale, or refuted with its counterexample) without asking it again, so a hints file whose decisions are all approved and proved asks nothing and lists nothing. main.rs builds the proof settings on every run, since they are part of every claim key.

Verified: 2 new tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs, by the own checker. Through the command they go: approve before a proof (listed as unproved); --prove (proved for K, nothing listed); a static rerun with the same settings (K kept) and with --unwind 8 (stale); a proof (proved again); a change to the new build (stale), then its proof (a new key). The other test covers a refuted approval listed with its counterexample, an approved method taking its pair's proof, and a relation no longer proposed going stale. All 33 alignment tests pass, as do the unit (185), foundations (3), skill (1) and conformance (9, 2 ignored) suites and the Python tests (23). The integration contract on this branch: 2 passed, 22 unsupported, 0 failed. Scores on 121-139 are unchanged, re-recorded under the new tool hash. Left for A5: what tells two proved relations apart (see Progress).

commits.summary: Alignment A5: proved relations with the same inputs are one candidate, told apart by a result no input gives; a question names an input that separates its candidates
commits.body:
Finishes A5, and with it every phase of the alignment stream. align --prove now collapses proved proposals that share an input mapping as well as those that share a relation (transitively): either way the old version gets the same observations on every input of the claim, which is the brief's rule for one candidate. What tells the collapsed relations apart is a new result no input produces, found by evaluating both relations with harness::expr over every old boolean and sampled new results (previous == (result > 0) against previous == (result != 0): -1), and is said in the proof's outcome, the kept hint's why and its question. Candidates with different inputs and different relations stay a question, with an input that separates two of them taken from a refuted proposal that has one's inputs and the other's relation, where such a proposal was tried.

Verified: 34 tests in lib/tests/alignment.rs (the test that held two such relations a question now asserts one candidate with -1 named; a new one covers a question with and without a separating input, and its collapse when the cross proposal is proved), the unit (185), foundations (3), skill (1) and conformance (9, 2 ignored) suites, the Python tests, and the integration contract (2 passed, 22 unsupported in other streams' parts, 0 failed). Scores on 121-139 unchanged, re-recorded under the new tool's hash. Status set to done; job 20261107-053806-alignment-a3-second-half-every-proposal stays for review, and its note says its proofs ran under the earlier collapse rule.
